title: GOAT Striker Analysis
GOAT Striker Analysis
text:
Who do we think is the best international striker? This site walks through the data quickly and honestly, then gives a clear pick at the end.
What you’ll see:

A plain explanation of the problem (goals vs. greatness)
A few smart metrics that actually matter
A short, evidence-backed pick for the top player

Follow the sections in the analysis for the full story — or skip to the conclusion to see our short answer.

title: Who Is the Greatest International Striker of All Time?
text: Who already stands out in the international scoring race? This chart gives the audience the first impression: the biggest names are visible immediately, and the takeaway is simple—raw totals create the shortlist, but they do not yet prove greatness. That is the bridge to the next question: if goals alone are not enough, what else should we measure?

text:
Limitations and next steps
How should we interpret the result with care? The dataset is strong but not complete, because it lacks minutes played, caps, and match context. The takeaway is that the ranking is useful but still a simplified view of greatness, and the next step is to add richer data if we want a more complete answer.

title: About
text:
This project is a sports analytics investigation that asks a focused question: who is the greatest international soccer striker of all time?


The dataset records every international goal by scorer, including:

match date,
national team,
scorer name,
goal minute,
penalty status,
goal type,
year and decade.

Each row is one goal, which means the analysis is built from the goals themselves rather than from match summaries.



The report evaluates the candidates with a professional lens:

raw scoring volume,
scoring quality through open-play share,
career consistency and efficiency,
era context,
a composite GOAT ranking model.




Greatest-striker discussions are common in soccer, but a strong analytic argument requires more than a leaderboard. This project emphasizes evidence, transparency, and the limits of the available data.



The current dataset does not include every context needed for a final historical judgement:

minutes played,
number of caps,
opponent strength,
match importance.

Those are valuable next steps for a deeper version of this project.
